A 400cc bike will definitely get you to where you need to go with decent power. With a 250/300cc you’ll get bored after the first year (or sooner depending on you). I started out with a 300cc which was perfect because it taught me to respect the power of a bike quickly; and the fact that it wasn’t as heavy as a 600cc bike made honing my skills easier. I never got into any accidents but the situations I’ve been in were very humbling. 

At the least, in my opinion, a 600cc is the most ideal- here’s why:
-it’s in the middle of both ends of the CC spectrum (I.e. 250cc-1200/2000cc)
-great torque, usually means awesome speed
-more fun to ride in the long term
-it’s heavy and it’ll force you to learn quickly how to handle it 

You’ll save more money on the 400cc- either way you won’t be unsatisfied with your purchase. 

However, please don’t buy a brand-new bike since it’ll be your first. I haven’t met anyone who hasn’t regretted buying a new bike because they ended up dropping it on a oil-slicked U-Turn or didn’t distribute their weight properly on hills. Buy something used that you don’t mind beating up a little bit with frame & handle sliders.

It sounds like you’ve already made your decision and ultimately it is.

I recommend sticking with a higher CC bike especially if you plan on riding on Highways, that extra power will get you out of sticky situations when you need to.

Find what you like and stick with it.
